findings.evidenceJa: 血液が流れるように、繋がった細い回路から
findings.governingReading: through the connected slender circuit, as though blood were flowing
findings.explanation: The bodily blood-flow simile governing the inaccessible memory connection disappears.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=その理由 o2o=1]混沌衝動
findings.governingReading: the chaotic impulse, written as such but read as “that reason”
findings.explanation: The pivotal double reading identifying his reason with a chaotic impulse is reduced to generic intentions.

findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで正体の掴めないヤツだった
findings.governingReading: he remained someone whose true nature could not be grasped until the end
findings.explanation: Others’ inability to understand what kind of person the savior was becomes simple suspicion.

findings.highlight: Greed, pride, selfishness, lust, vengeance, or devotion
findings.evidenceJa: 富豪、名声、我欲、復讐、献身
findings.explanation: Wealth and fame become moral vices, lust is invented, and the list’s contrast between legible motives is reorganized.

findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=さいしょのみち char=4]原初の心
findings.governingReading: his primal heart, read as “the first path”
findings.explanation: The double reading joining an unchanged inner origin to the route from start to finish disappears.
Critics attack the narrow scope of his values; the English instead attacks idealism as blind, altering the nature of the accusation.

findings.evidenceJa: あっけなく死んでしまった
findings.governingReading: he died all too abruptly at their hands
findings.explanation: The abrupt, bathetic ease of the savior’s end disappears.

findings.highlight: used this scenery as his weapon
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=ささえ char=2]武器にして
findings.governingReading: made this scene his weapon, read as his support
findings.explanation: The written weapon/read support double function of the inner landscape is lost.

findings.highlight: for strangers who shouldn’t have meant anything to him
findings.evidenceJa: どうでもいい誰かの為に
findings.governingReading: for some person of no concern to him
findings.explanation: Impersonal lack of self-interest becomes a normative claim that strangers ought not matter to him.
